desc: The local temple complexes have been expanded with vaulted gardens, serene places which house freshwater wells.
name: Temple Sanctuaries

desc: Great investment has gone into massive central squares that abound with religious artwork, are kept bare of excess waste and usury, and supply water to locals.
name: Monumental Squares

desc: People with means are encouraged by authorities to give surplus food and wealth to the less fortunate, typically during holy days.
name: Charitable Customs

desc: The very poor, widows and the elderly are given modest boarding and some care in simple accommodations.
name: Poorhouses

desc: Almshouses and other civic needs that serve the wretched are well-serviced by official ministers of some means.
name: Benevolent Ministries

desc: All through the land, the needy want for nought. Gracious accommodations house would-be vagrants, hospitals tend to the sick and elderly, and generous allowances are made for poor peasants.
name: Charitable Institutions

desc: Aristocratic fighters of long service have been given generous local plots, and interest in serving loyally has increased here accordingly.
name: Veterans' Smallholdings

desc: Those of the aristocratic warrior class who do not die on the battlefield live in comfort, their granted holdings allowing them to recruit and arm themselves amply.
name: Martial Estates

desc: Many local villages are given over to knightly officers as personal holdings, allowing them to gather strength and wealth at the expense of the other classes.
name: Village Fiefdoms

desc: A sizeable share of local taxes are delivered unto minor warrior aristocrats, the title-holders to field and settlement alike. Their mighty retinues, however, still serve.
name: Vast Martial Holdings

desc: A place of worship ruled by the clergy, surrounded by a town of faithful peasants.

desc:
A university is a place of higher learning, reserved for those of good standing and wealth who are deemed worthy enough. It attracts scholars and scientists who debate, study, scribe, and ultimately pool their knowledge within its walls.

The Al-Azhar University is named in honor of Fatimah, the daughter of Muhammad, who was often called 'al-Zahra' (the Luminous).

name: Al-Azhar University

desc:
Founded by merchants and migrants from Kairouan, the sprawling complex has become one of the most prestigious centers of higher learning in the western Islamic world. It attracts scholars from far away regions and educates local elites in the finer subjects.
The madrasa is composed of several halls and rooms - offering a bed and rest to foreign students with Sahn as the central courtyard of public discussion.

desc: This eagle's nest, perched atop a lofty crag, was built by the Justanids to serve as a fortress redoubt of their beleaguered realm. With its awe-inspiring setting and strong ramparts, it is near-impregnable by all accounts, and could prove an ideal stronghold for any warlike faction or sect that would thrive in such an isolated location.

lines: +0.2 Character Capital County Monthly Control Change Add /month

name: Alamut Castle

desc: Perched atop a lofty crag, this castle has long served as a remote mountain redoubt. It has now been rebuilt into a formidable fedayeen fortress, housing libraries, laboratories and tranquil gardens among the imposing fortifications. To some, it is a place of bloodshed and war, to others a place of spiritual repose - or perhaps both.

lines: +0.2 Character Capital County Monthly Control Change Add /month

name: Alamut Fortress

desc: Rising like the bow of a ship from a rocky crag, this fortress is an awe-inspiring sight. As majestic as it is impenetrable, it is the greatest of all castles in the kingdom of castles — Castile.
name: Alcázar of Segovia

desc: The Alhambra is a fortress built upon the remains of an ancient Roman fortification. While it is serviceable as a defensive structure, with the right investments it could be turned into something more...
effects: Unlocks:Reduced Cost for hosting Feast in this Holding:…
name: Alhambra Fortress Ruins

desc: The Alhambra has since its days as a mere Roman ruin been upgraded to a royal palace befitting an emperor! A shining example of local architecture, the color of the buildings in contrast with the surrounding woods lead poets to describe it as "a pearl set in emeralds."
effects: Unlocks:Reduced Cost for hosting Feast in this Holding:…
name: Royal Palace of Alhambra

conds: faith lacks: Buildings of this Faith need only half as much Luxury Items and Luxury Consumables, and gain a smaller benefit from them
needs.name: Silk

desc: A great palace-fortress built on the Saría plain, the Aljafería is a testament to the power and wealth of Zaragoza. Imposing and splendid in equal measure; it is both an intimidating fortification and a pinnacle of Iberian architecture.
name: Aljafería

desc: While Pagan has thousands of pagodas, temples, and shrines littered throughout the city and the surrounding plains, the Ananda Temple stands as a crowning achievement among them. The perfectly dimensioned structure contains many unique plaques and stone images. It is a place of worship and a center of learning to educate the people in religious ethos.
effects: Unlocks:Increases Legitimacy gain and Piety gain for Funeral Activities Hosted in this Holding

lines: +0.1 Character Capital County Monthly Control Change Add /month

name: Ananda Temple

desc: Angkor Wat is a massive temple complex dedicated to the deity Vishnu. It is designed to be a representation of Mount Meru, home of the gods in Hindu mythology. The complex is surrounded by an impressive moat and has several galleried temples, overflowing with religious art, sculptures and reliefs.
name: Angkor Wat

desc:
The Basilica of Sant'Apollinare Nuovo has only gained its current name recently, when the relics of Saint Apollinaris were transferred from the neighboring Basilica in Classe. Its history, however, is much longer.
First consecrated in the early 6th century by King Theodoric of the Ostrogoths as an Arian church, the building has seen many renovations both in structure and decoration while maintaining its unique style — an elegant mixture of western and eastern art — and its amazing Byzantine mosaics.

lines: +0.1 Character Capital County Monthly Control Change Add /month

modifiers.cond: if culture has: Cathedral Buildings also give Civic Tax

name: Sant'Apollinare Nuovo

desc: It is said that prince Siyavusha built this massive fortress when the world was young. Three thousand years later, it was restored by the Bukhara Khudas, the ancient rulers of this region, and it has been in use ever since. Travelers come from near and far to admire the construction, with seven great pillars mirroring the seven stars of the Big Dipper, but it is a fortification first and foremost, intimidating in its splendor.
name: Ark of Bukhara

desc: Perched atop a lofty crag, this castle has long served as a remote mountain redoubt. It has now been rebuilt into a formidable fedayeen fortress, housing libraries, laboratories and tranquil gardens among the imposing fortifications. To some, it is a place of bloodshed and war, to others a place of spiritual repose - or perhaps both.

lines: +0.2 Character Capital County Monthly Control Change Add /month

name: Hashshashin Castle IV

desc: Known as the "Mother Temple of Bali," Besakih is the island's most significant and holiest Hindu temple complex. It is located on the slopes of Mount Agung, Bali's tallest volcano and sacred mountain. It is the island's religious and cultural heart, hosting grand ceremonies for all.
name: Besakih Temple

desc:
The Beta Giyorgis has been carved entirely out of a warm, red volcanic rock. Surrounding it are a dozen other sister temples and buildings, meant to represent both Earthly and Heavenly Jerusalem. This is living proof of the link between the Holy kingdom and this land.
Burrowed deep within the rock, the main hall of the church is lavishly painted with beautiful frescoes, while holy icons adorn the walls.
name: St George of Lalibela

requirements.name: Christianity (or syncretic) or Holy site of your faith

desc: Borobudur is a massive Buddhist temple consisting of nine stone platforms stacked on top of each other, topped by a central dome. The temple is decorated with thousands of reliefs and hundreds of Buddha statues.
name: Borobudur

desc:
The Boudha Stupa of Kathmandu, also known as Jarung Kashor and Khāsa Chaitya, is one of the largest stupas in Buddhism, and may be the birthplace of what became the Tibetan branch of Buddhism. Its enormous dome and mandala houses the remains of multiple buddhas and innumerable sacred relics of various shapes and forms. 

Due to its placement on an ancient trade route between Nepal and Tibet, travellers and merchants frequently stop by to rest and pray.
effects: Unlocks:Increases Legitimacy gain and Piety gain for Funeral Activities Hosted in this Holding
name: Boudhanath

requirements.name: Holy site of your faith or Eastern (or syncretic)

desc: The Brihadeeswarar Temple is dedicated to the Hindu deity Shiva and is one of the largest South Indian temples built in the ornate Dravidian architectural style. The name of the temple is a Sanskrit composite word that roughly translates as "Temple of the Great Lord Shiva."
effects: Unlocks:Increases Legitimacy gain and Piety gain for Funeral Activities Hosted in this Holding
name: Brihadeeswarar Temple

desc: The Daibutsu of Kamakura is a venerable bronze statue of the Amitābha Buddha, weighing several tons and decorated with gilded details. It is enclosed by a great hall inspired by the temples of the southwest and surrounded by thirty-two lotus petals.
effects: Unlocks:Increases Legitimacy gain and Piety gain for Funeral Activities Hosted in this Holding

lines: +0.15 Prestige per Powerful Vassal on the Council /month

name: Great Buddha of Kamakura

desc: Carved out of the mountainside, the massive Buddhas of Bamian loom over any visitors. While the area surrounding them is no longer the thriving center of Buddhist learning as it once was, there's still numerous Buddhist pilgrims and scholars visiting the statues. A shrewd Dharmic ruler might even be able to pull a profit from the pilgrims, in addition to gaining some personal insights.
name: Buddhas of Bamian

desc:
The Burkhan Khaldun is the most imposing of the Khentii Mountains.
Said to be the birthplace of many Mongolian heroes, its slopes are covered in ovoos and many sacrifices are made in the hopes of gaining its favor.

lines: +25% County Fertility Growth in Mountains Terrain

name: Burkhan Khaldun

desc: Situated just west of Gaeseong city at the mouth of the Ryeseong river, the port of Byeokran is the most direct route for foreign goods and travelers to enter the Korean peninsula, avoiding the northern borders and mountain ranges.
name: Byeokran Port

desc:
The Byzantine influence on this building is strong: a small church with baptistery, in red bricks nested upon naked rocks, with an "inscribed cross" plan and a rich decoration of fresco cycles, dominating the valley of the Stilaro stream.
The church is an isolated gem in the middle of hostile nature, where man can feel closer to God.
name: Cattolica di Stilo

desc: The markets of the great city of Cháng'ān, Perpetual Peace, bustle with all manner of trade, and are an essential stop for nearly all commerce heading both in and out of China.

modifiers.cond: if culture has: Silk Road Market Buildings give additional Commerce Tax

desc: Originally based in Taga, the Chinjufu is the fortified center of the imperial pacification efforts in northern Japan, overseen by a special commander with responsibility for the region's defense and taxation.
name: Chinjufu District

desc: This geological formation is characterized by a great number of rounded, conical hills that stretch uniformly across the landscape. They are cloaked in a layer of grass that - during the dry season - turns a vivid hue of brown and orange, giving the terrain an unusual autumnal flush.
effects: Unlocks:Increases Hunt Sighting Chance and Hunt Success Chance forHunt Activities Hosted in this Holding
name: Slopes of Russet

desc:
The Holy Cross has long conquered this magnificent structure, vanquishing the pagan cult to the virgin goddess Athena.
Nowadays, it holds the shrines to Maria Parthenos, Mother of God and only Virgin worthy of the name Holy.

lines: +0.05 Character Capital County Monthly Control Change Add /month

name: Temple of the Theotokos

desc:
The holy temple of mighty Athena stands proudly once again, uncontaminated by silly superstitions.
These majestic columns and walls, raised more than 1000 years ago, have withstood the test of time and still protect the homes of the faithful from above, a silent symbol of the blessing of the Virgin Goddess who named the city.

lines: +0.05 Character Capital County Monthly Control Change Add /month

name: Parthenon

desc:
The Cilician Gates are a pass through the Taurus Mountains that connect the Cilician plains with the Anatolian plateau.
Since time immemorial, the pass has been fortified, and controlling it meant controlling one of the main commercial and military arteries of Asia Minor and the Middle East.
name: Cilician Gates

desc: Built along the northern slopes of the Phoenix Hill, the imperial citadel serves as the seat of the court and its administration, hosting countless scholars and officials in its cavernous halls and corridors. Though not as vast as the palaces of the northern capitals, the refinement and elegance of its terraced gardens and pavilions more than matches them.
name: Imperial Citadel of Lin'an

effects: Unlocks:Reduced Cost for hosting Feast in this Holding:…
name: Citadel of Aleppo

desc: After having gone through major reconstruction, the Citadel of Aleppo has been significantly fortified and turned into a proper palatial city!
effects: Unlocks:Reduced Cost for hosting Feast in this Holding:…
name: Reconstructed Citadel of Aleppo

desc: A citadel that serves as a military base for local armies and is greatly fortified to help repel invaders.
name: Đai La Citadel

desc: The Imperial Citadel acts as a fortress and royal residence. The citadel complex includes three sectors, the primary fortification, the imperial city, and the Forbidden City.
name: Imperial Citadel of Thăng Long

desc: Originally built by the Romans in days of old, these massive walls were significantly expanded under the reign of Wamba, king of the Visigoths. The early Arabic rulers widened them even further, creating a defensive system fit for the City of Kings.
name: City Walls of Toledo

desc:
A gift of land and rights, in exchange for eternal salvation. That is the covenant which has been formed between the monastic community of Cluny and the local lord.
Over time, it has grown into a lively and influential community, free of secular interference, enforcing Benedictine discipline far and wide.

Under its many red roofs, monks pray, labor and illuminate manuscripts - a model for others to emulate throughout the continent.

desc:
What were once a few monachal homes have been replaced by a sprawling religious complex.
To cement this legacy its abbots have embarked on a colossal building project, the Maior Ecclesia. Meant to be the largest church in Christendom the five naves are longer than those of the Vatican and its massive stone vaults are an architectural achievement, teeming with towers and roofs.

desc: The oldest and most influential of all Confucian temples, this vast complex of halls and courtyards has been a model of reference and inspiration for temple builders all across China and beyond, with its harmonious geometrical layout and refined details. Nearby lies a quiet forest where the tombs of Confucius and his descendants have been laid to rest, forming an important place of pilgrimage for devotees.
effects: Unlocks:Increases Legitimacy gain and Piety gain for Funeral Activities Hosted in this Holding
name: Temple of Confucius

desc: Scholars built an academy among Mount Culai's peaks to study Confucian texts in seclusion. Its halls echoed with debates on harmonizing nature and governance.

desc:
This mosque has a venerable story to tell. Here many centuries of spirituality and wondrous ingenuity are stratified one over the other as it is built on top of a Roman temple and an early Christian Basilica.
The building is renowned for its opulent and colorful marbles, as well as its golden mosaics pieced together by artists from as far as Constantinople.
name: Great Mosque of Damascus

requirements.name: Islam (or syncretic) or Holy site of your faith

desc: The Danevirke is an extensive earthwork fortification built to prevent incursions from the continent into Danish territories and has been expanded multiple times since its original construction.
name: Danevirke

desc: A revered temple in Luy Lâu, marks the spot where monks from far-off lands first came together. The brick tower, relics, and mummified masters that remain there embody centuries of devotion to Buddhism.
name: Dâu Temple

desc: The town of Dazaifu is the imperial court's administrative center on distant Kyūshū. Established to oversee the island's defense, facilitate overseas trade, and host foreign dignitaries, governorship of Dazaifu is a common career stepping stone of ambitious bureaucrats.

lines: +0.1 Character Capital County Monthly Control Change Add /month

modifiers.cond: if government has: Is Administrative

name: Dazaifu Office

desc: This site has been favored for astronomical observation for centuries, due to its geomantic qualities and symbolic geographic centrality within China. The current structure, a complex trapezoidal shape, serves as a vast sundial, with the tall central ruler casting its shadow into the trench that divides the platform, and marking the passage of the sun.

The palace has all the luxuries to compete with the greatness of the Constantinopolitan halls, and it's worthy of only the richest and most influential of governors.

lines: +10% Stress Loss per Level of Devotion

name: Dieng Plateau

desc: The Dome of the Rock is situated in the center of the Temple Mount, in the place where the Temple of Solomon and the Jewish Second Temple stood. desc:
The monastery is dedicated to the preservation of the relics of Venerable Luke of Steiris, the hermit monk.
The holy remains are said to exude a miraculous oil, and attract countless pilgrims who sleep by the tomb in order to be healed by incubation. The inner decoration is praised throughout the Eastern Mediterranean for its quality and lavishness, as the finest artists of the age have enriched it with mosaics, icons, chandeliers, carvings, and cloths.

name: Hotin Fort

desc: An impressive Fortress that makes the old fort pale in comparison. The fortifications have been expanded across the centuries to include high stone walls, a wide moat, and several massive towers. This defensive structure will hold most besiegers at bay with ease.
name: Hotin Fortress

desc: The House of Wisdom contains a vast collection of books, and the scribes therein work tirelessly both day and night to translate even more great works of literature. The sources vary from Greek, Persian, Indian and many more — truly, it contains the entire world's knowledge! A shining beacon of human knowledge! And comfortably far from the illiterate horsemen of the steppe...

desc: This sanctuary houses the remains of Ali ar-Rida, celebrated by some Shiites as the eighth imam, who was martyred in this land. The ever-expanding complex includes his shrine as well as prayer halls, a library and a bazaar, growing in an eclectic but glorious fashion with the ebb and flow of pilgrims and caravans.
name: Sanctuary of Imam Reza

Set near the flood-prone plain, it has become known as a warden against the rising tides to the local citizens.

name: Iron Pillar of Delhi

desc: The Iron Pillar of Dhar is constructed from the molten-down arms of an entire army. The craftsmanship is truly astounding, bringing glory upon the dynasty which holds it.

The temple is the most sacred in the land, a labyrinthine complex of courtyards and monastic residencies traversed by cavernous corridors and halls covered in yak butter.

Man's dominion over hostile nature here is still very feeble, though; the monasteries are extremely hard to reach, mostly relying only on ladders, ropes, hand-hauling, and prayers, as the fall in case of equipment's failure is lethal.

desc:
In 708, Saint Aubert, Bishop of Avranches, saw in a dream a vision of the Archangel Michael, instructing him to build an oratory upon a nearby tidal island. Aubert at first ignored this vision, attributing it to a trick by the Devil. Eventually the Archangel managed to convince him - according to legend by poking a hole in his skull with a touch, and the bishop ordered the contruction of a new sanctuary on Mont Tombe. 

Thus begins the history of Mont-Saint-Michel.

desc: Rising above Lake Venado, Mount Apo's name means "revered elder" in Lumad languages. It is a shortened form of Apo Sandawa, the spirit of the sacred mountain, also called "Elder Sandawa" or "Grandfather Sandawa." Rituals for Apo Sandawa are performed by the tribe's shaman who is seen as a medium for ancestor spirits.
name: Mount Apo

desc: Christian communities have inhabited this promontory since at least the times of Emperor Constantine I, and monks from Mount Athos already took part in the Seventh Council of Nicaea. However, no proper monastic community or permanent buildings exist yet.
name: Mount Athos

desc: The arrival of a monk called Athanasios to Mount Athos sets into motion the foundation of several monasteries throughout the peninsula: first of all, Great Lavra and Vatopedi, both dedicated to the Annunciation. With proper monasteries, the local monastic life is given order and rules.
name: Mount Athos

desc:
The popularity of Mount Athos as a monastic center, based on the many concessions offered to it by the lay power, its autonomous statutory, the truly isolated lifestyle, and its flourishing production of icons, has ensured a continuous stream of new joining monks for centuries.
As the number of monks grew, so did the number of monasteries. Twenty monasteries currently exist on Mt. Athos, making it one of the largest and more influential monastic communities in the area.
name: Mount Athos

desc: The lofty peak of Mount Baekdu is said to be the origin of all the mountains of the Korean peninsula, and its heights are a sacred place among the region's many faiths and peoples.
name: Mount Baekdu

desc: A great, snow-capped pinnacle steeped in ancient lore, Mount Damavand is said to be the prison of the monstrous tyrant Zahhāk, where he will abide until the end of the world. Many heroes of old have performed great feats on this mountain, and to those who travel there today, its mighty presence seem to touch their very souls. A dormant volcano, its slopes are dotted by hot springs where weary travelers can stop and relax, pondering the deeds of the ancients.
name: Mount Damavand

desc: The lone, towering, snow-capped peak of Fujisan marks the passage into eastern Japan and is a sight famed throughout the islands, drawing travelers and pilgrims, and granting repose to all who gaze upon it. Among the most sacred Shintō mountains, Fuji is home to Konohanasakuya-hime, goddess of volcanoes, the cherry blossom, and life's ephemeral delicacy.
name: Mount Fuji

desc: The key-hole shaped mounds at Mozu are said to house past emperors of old. For ships in the nearby bay they are a notable landmark as well as a reminder of times past.

desc: Many structures compose the temple complex, all brick-built and adorned with sandstone detailings. At the center rise the great stupas of Mahligai and Tuo, the former tall and slender, the latter vast like a mountain, towering above the smaller shrines and terraces around them.

desc: A Mongolian palace, serving both as a military and cultural center in equal measure. Its crowning glory stands as a fountain in the shape of a silver tree, where different kinds of wine flow from the serpents that entwine the statue.

desc: A pinnacle of Cham architecture, the Po Klong Garai temple is said to be built to honor the legendary king of the same name. It has three distinct brick towers and an impressive sculpture of the god Shiva as its primary art piece.
name: Po Klong Garai Temple

desc: This great stepped pyramid rises from the jungle like a holy mountain, each of its seven terraces holding increasingly ornate shrines and altars. The upper sanctuary crowns the structure, and protects within the sacred lingam of Shiva, the center of a complex axial plan of religious design.
effects: Unlocks:Increases Legitimacy gain and Piety gain for Funeral Activities Hosted in this Holding

desc: The Qianling Mausoleum is primarily the tomb of Emperor Gaozong and Empress Wu Zetian, though several other members of the Li family is buried here as well. The burial mound is protected by a rectangular wall and the many stone statues that adorn the landscape is one of the mausoleum's most recognizable features.
name: Qianling Mausoleum

desc: Quanzhou's port attracts foreign merchants from far and wide. Traders are known to come from Arabia and Anatolia, Japan and Korea, and everything in-between. This influx of trade vessels ensures that local industries are booming and it has made Quanzhou the foremost shipbuilder in the region.
name: Quanzhou Seaport

desc: The mighty Iron Pillar of Delhi stands as a symbol to the glory of King Chandragupta II, though subsequent rulers have also etched their names into it. Despite having stood for a long time, there's no trace of rust – a testament to the skill of Indian ironsmiths!
name: Iron Pillar of Delhi

desc:
The Quwwat-ul-Islam, a grand mosque surrounding the old site that was the Iron Pillar of Delhi, crowned with a truly enormous minaret called the Qutb Minar. 

A magnificient monument to the power of the rulers of Delhi.
name: Qutb Minar

desc: The Creator themselves seem to have painted these ridges in a rainbow of colors. Bands of red, white, yellow, gray, orange and yet stranger hues tint the rocky, tranquil landscape. Local rulers will often take guest hunting here, to see this sublime wonder.

desc: The monolithic Rock of Gibraltar overlooks a narrow strait that is the gateway to the Mediterranean Sea. It was one of the Pillars of Hercules in antiquity, considered to mark the end of the known world. Looking at it now, you cannot help but wonder what lies beyond.
name: Rock of Gibraltar

desc: Built by the Romans long ago, the great Walls of Lugo remain an impressive sight. Pilgrims pass their five gates on the road to Santiago de Compostela, making the journey even more profound.
name: Roman Walls of Lugo

desc:
An unassuming monastery in the middle of the desert, but with a heavy history. The first monastic structure was, in fact, ordered to be built by Emperor Constantine's mother on the site of the apparition of the Burning Bush to Moses. Emperor Justinian financed its expansion into the current fortified monastery, also enclosing the Well of Moses. Only centuries after its foundation did the spoils of Saint Catherine arrive at the monastery, changing its name.
The monastery has always been among the most ancient and prolific scriptoria and icon-making centers.

lines: +0.2 Character Capital County Monthly Control Change Add /month

name: Saint Catherine's Monastery

desc:
According to tradition, Lazarus of Bethany, once raised from the dead by Christ, was buried in the town of Larnaca upon his second death.
The tomb was lost for centuries but, upon its retrieval, Emperor Leo VI had the saint's remains moved to Constantinople and this imposing church built on top of the grave.

lines: +0.05 Character Capital County Monthly Control Change Add /month

name: Church of Saint Lazarus

desc: The Great Stupa was built by the Mauryan Emperor Ashoka in the third century BC, near the site of his wedding with his wife Devi. The grandiose structure housing relics of the Buddha is one of the oldest of its kind, and it is also famed for its intricately carved torana gateways.
effects: Unlocks:Increases Legitimacy gain and Piety gain for Funeral Activities Hosted in this Holding

A university is a place of higher learning, reserved for those of good standing and wealth who are deemed worthy enough. It attracts scholars and scientists who debate, study, scribe, and ultimately pool their knowledge within its walls.

The University of Sankoré, which started out as a Mosque, transformed into a center of learning after acquiring a wealth of books from traveling merchants.

name: Shah-i-Zinda

desc: A vast necropolis of mausoleums, tall gates and domed passages clad in turquoise tiles, The Living King is the burial site of the prophet's cousin and many other great lords of old. The complex is ever-expanding and sublime, eerie and impressive in equal measure.

desc: Some locals will tell you that before there was money, Kashgar already had the Sunday Bazaar. Walking between the stalls of the market, it certainly feels that way — it's impossible to imagine a time without this place.

desc: Scattered across the valleys of Central Sulawesi lie many megalithic figures and icons raised by the local people for rituals and to honor the spirits. These effigies, known as arcas, are carved with minimalist precision, their forms traced with subtle and elegant lines.
name: Sulawesi Megaliths

desc: The warm white sands of its beaches and the vibrant blue of the waters that lazily lap its shores belie the bustling commerce that serves as the lifeblood of Lamu. Long connected to trade across the ocean, goods from the western and eastern ends of the known world can be bought and sold here.
name: Lamu Trade Ports

desc: Perched atop a rocky island surrounded by steep cliffs, Mombasa enjoys a naturally defensible position that still remains uniquely accessible to maritime traffic.
name: Port of Mombasa

desc: Located on the northern edge of the Swahili heartlands, Pate Island was one of the first Swahili regions introduced to Islam and thus to Middle Eastern trade networks.
name: Pate Island Trade Ports

desc: The reefs, beaches, and mangrove forests of Pemba Island provide an abundance of inlets and resources for the people of Pemba, making it a natural entrepôt of the Zanj.
name: Pemba Trade Ports

desc: The island of Unguja's sandy shores sheltered by coral islets make it a perfect haven for ships. Traders from across the Indian Ocean come to enjoy Unguja's natural strengths as a center of maritime commerce.
name: Zanzibar Trade Ports

desc: The venerable market of Tabriz has served as the great hub of commerce since time immemorial. Its walls are decorated with colorful tiles and tinted plasters, reflecting the wealth and prestige of this ancient marketplace.

modifiers.cond: if culture has: Silk Road Market Buildings give additional Commerce Tax

desc: Age has not sapped Tabriz's august and ancient marketplace of any vitality; if anything, the venerable bazaar seems more lively than ever before.

desc: Angkor Wat is a massive temple complex dedicated to the deity Vishnu. It is designed to be a representation of Mount Meru, home of the gods in Hindu mythology. The complex is surrounded by an impressive moat and has several galleried temples, overflowing with religious art, sculptures and reliefs.
effects: Unlocks:Increases Legitimacy gain and Piety gain for Funeral Activities Hosted in this Holding
name: Angkor Wat

desc:
The Colosseum is one of the largest amphitheaters ever built and has hosted countless spectacles such as gladiatorial combat, animal hunts and even reconstructed sea battles. Its construction was started by the Roman emperor Vespasian in AD 72 and was completed in AD 80 under his successor, Titus.

Despite its vibrant history, its primary use today is for harvesting marble and bronze for use elsewhere.
name: The Colosseum

desc: The Friday Mosque, or the Jameh Mosque of Esfahan, was built during the Umayyad dynasty. It is said that the Caliph personally made one of the pillars in the mosque. Before becoming a mosque, it is said that it used to be a house of worship for Zoroastrians.

desc: The Tower of London is a castle that serves as both a vital fortification and a prison. The central tower is called the 'White Tower' and houses the ruling class. The position of the Tower of London means that it's vital to the defense of the entire County.

desc: Over two hundred large kilns cover the site, the largest center of celadon production in the region. The ceramics fired here are known for their coarse, hard-fired texture and distinctive yellow-green glaze, and are traded all across the markets of Southeast Asia.

desc: This ancient tomb of white limestone is said to be the resting place of Batsheba, the mother of king Solomon, exalted by many faiths. Women tend to the site, and only women are allowed to enter the tomb's dark interior. They seldom speak of what they have seen inside. The waters nearby are said to be blessed, and can cure those who have been bitten by mad dogs.
name: Tomb of Batsheba

desc: This ancient lighthouse is said to have been based on its more famous sister in Alexandria. Having guided seafarers for untold centuries, it remains important to Galicia's coastal trade. Some claim that you can glimpse Ireland's green coast from the top of this lonely tower, but gazing out, you see only endless sea.
name: Farum Brigantium

desc: An achievement of engineering worthy of fame, this white marble sentinel stands tall and proud over the city.
name: Tower of Pisa

desc: This white marble belltower stands tall over the city, although perhaps not quite as tall as it could have been. That it remains standing at all is a testament to the skill of its builders.
name: Leaning Tower of Pisa

desc:
Constructed by the early Chalukya dynasty these sacred caves have been cut deep into an imperious sandstone formation. Inside lies a most holy and silent inner world.
A triumphal gate leads pilgrims into the monolithic face of the mountain. The caves are decorated with idols from all the major faiths of India.
name: Vatapi Caves

desc: The Visby City Wall protects the city from external threats such as raiders or Danes. It also efficiently keeps out tax collectors sent by the Thing of Gotland! To get to the riches within, assailants must first deal with a plethora of towers all manned by archers.
name: Visby Ringmur

desc:
This citadel is a grandiose, impenetrable system of walls and towers. It protects the Danube bend and controls its rich trade. 
Visegrad citadel is composed of a lower portion with a powerful hexagonal tower facing the river, and an upper acropolis surmounting the tall hill. The massive triangular fortification works as a residence as well as an opulent hunting lodge.

desc: The Walls of Benin are a massive series of earthworks (Iya in the Edo language), that encircle the entirety of Benin. The walls are built of a ditch and dike structure, with an inner moat and an exterior rampart.
name: Walls of Benin

desc: The Walls of Genoa were built in the 9th century after the city was granted significant autonomy. The walls, together with the protection of the coastline, allow the area to develop and prosper.
name: Walls of Genoa

desc:
In the Thuringian forest, perched atop a great, rocky precipice, this fortress controls all movement of goods and men through the region.
A heavy barbican guards the only access to the castle, and tall white walls snake through the crevices of the mountain. The Palas, is the most important building in the complex, a massive hall of cold stone warmed by the many hearths within.
